answer: Persistent Attention Anchor. Each identity must periodically solve a challenge tied to the live state of a shared queue, signing a checkpoint that advances only if the prior checkpoint was witnessed. This forces a continuous compute-and-latency spend per identity, not a one-time fee. Splitting identities multiplies that recurring cost, producing a spiral of diminishing returns. Attackers must forge sustained real-time presence across every clone, making mass fabrication economically irrational.
